decisive_spans.text: There were confluent erythematous, edematous plaques in the bilateral periorbital areas (left more than right), studded with numerous 2– to 3-mm pustules, some coalescing into “lakes of pus.” A few pustules were also noted in the perioral area.

response.rationale: The patient's presentation with confluent erythematous, edematous plaques and pustules, particularly in the periorbital and perioral areas, strongly supports Perioral dermatitis. While the patient used steroids, the absence of steroid-induced atrophy makes steroid-induced rosacea-like dermatitis less likely. The other diagnoses are not as well supported by the specific distribution and morphology of the rash.
